      B[i] = (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 0.5;\n    }\n    \n    // Compute A = B * B^T\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum += B[i * n + k] * B[j * n + k];\n            }\n            A[i * n + j] = sum;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // Add diagonal dominance to ensure positive definiteness\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        A[i * n + i] += n;\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateCholesky(const std::vector<double>& L, const std::vector<double>& A_orig, const size_t n) {\n    // Validate by computing L * L^T and comparing with original matrix\n    \n    std::vector<double> reconstructed(n * n);\n    \n    // Compute L * L^T\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum += L[i * n + k] * L[j * n + k];\n            }\n            reconstructed[i * n + j] = sum;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // Compare with original\n    double maxError = 0.0;\n    double relError = 0.0;\n    \n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        const double error = fabs(reconstructed[i] - A_orig[i]);\n        maxError = std::max(maxError, error);\n        \n        const double rel = error / (fabs(A_orig[i]) + 1e-10);\n        relError = std::max(relError, rel);\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Max absolute error: %.10e\\n\", maxError);\n    printf(\"Max relative error: %.10e\\n\", relError);\n    \n    // Check if error is Before deciding further, I need to check what's actually available in this environment—nvcc, MPI, and GPU hardware—and keep in mind that the final numerical results must stay close to the reference even though a blocked algorithm changes floating-point operation order slightly.\n\nThen I'm thinking about summation order: the original Cholesky–Banachiewicz implementation computes each element as a strictly sequential dot product over increasing k, so if I preserve that per-element order exactly, results should match the original closely even with FMA contraction differences. Parallelism can still be introduced across the (i,j) pairs while keeping each individual dot-product loop sequential, which preserves correctness guarantees.\n\nBut the real issue is row-level dependency: each element depends on completed earlier rows and earlier elements in the same row, making row-wise Cholesky inherently sequential within a row — this is what pushes me toward reconsidering the approach entirely.\n\nA more realistic design would be a blocked, right-looking Cholesky: factor the diagonal block, apply triangular solves to the panel, then update the trailing matrix via GEMM/SYRK, distributed block-cyclically across MPI ranks with GPU acceleration for the trailing updates and OpenMP for panel work. This changes summation order and therefore numerical results slightly, but should still pass a relative-error validation threshold even though exact hash comparisons will differ from the original.\n\nI also need to think about the matrix generation step — using rand_r with a fixed seed to build B, then computing A = B·B^T — which isn't timed but still costs O(n³) for large n. The random generation itself should stay sequential to preserve the same matrix, but the GEMM to form A and the final validation L·L^T can both be parallelized. I'm also weighing what default/hidden test sizes might be used, and sketching an MPI design using 1D block-column cyclic distribution with a right-looking algorithm, where the panel owner factors its diagonal block and broadcasts results to other ranks.\n\nI'm now thinking through storage layout — full-height column blocks per rank versus replicating the whole matrix — settling on distributed column-block storage for scalability, and planning the GPU side using a custom tiled CUDA GEMM kernel rather than cuBLAS to avoid adding a new dependency. Given the scope of this, I realize I need to actually check whether the environment has nvcc, mpicxx, and a GPU available before committing to this approach, since the build would otherwise fail.\n\n","time":{"start":1793044099456,"end":1793044113575},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793044506827,"sessionID":"ses_e863e65faffe1w255t7oeq86WJ","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01YWpNHrf8wN4Ft7dXxPTwWx","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r3/cholesky/cholesky.cpp","content":"// Hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA Cholesky decomposition benchmark.\n//\n// Algorithm: blocked left-looking Cholesky (A = L * L^T, row-major, lower L).\n// For every element L(i,j) the dot product over k < j is accumulated by a single\n// sequential fused-multiply-add chain, exactly as in the sequential reference.\n// The blocked formulation keeps that chain intact: the k < J0 part for a block of\n// columns J is computed by a k-ascending GPU GEMM, and the in-block remainder\n// continues the same accumulator on the host. Results are therefore bit-identical\n// to the sequential algorithm (on FMA-contracting builds).\n//\n// Parallelization:\n//   MPI    - the rows below each column block are split across ranks; every rank\n//            receives the finished block column (MPI_Allgatherv) and keeps a full\n//            copy of L on the host and on its GPU.\n//   CUDA   - each rank drives one GPU (round-robin over local ranks). The\n//            dominant O(n^3) work, the GEMM over finished columns, runs on the GPU.\n//   OpenMP - host-side work: diagonal-block factorization, triangular solves of\n//            the rows below the block, matrix generation and validation.\n\n#include <mpi.h>\n#include <omp.h>\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n#include <unistd.h>\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\nnamespace {\n\n// Width of a column block (panel). Also the GPU GEMM's N dimension.\nconstexpr size_t kPanel = 128;\n\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                          \\\n    do {                                                                          \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                                \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                                \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__,      \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_));                                    \\\n            MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);                                         \\\n        }                                                                         \\\n    } while (0)\n\nstruct Dist {\n    int rank = 0;\n    int size = 1;\n    int localRank = 0;\n    int localSize = 1;\n};\n\n// Index of the first entry of packed lower-triangular row i (row i has i+1 entries).\ninline size_t tri(size_t i) { return i * (i + 1) / 2; }\n\n// Balanced contiguous partition of [lo, hi) into `parts` pieces; returns piece `part`.\ninline void partition(size_t lo, size_t hi, int parts, int part, size_t& b, size_t& e) {\n    const size_t len = hi - lo;\n    b = lo + len * static_cast<size_t>(part) / parts;\n    e = lo + len * static_cast<size_t>(part + 1) / parts;\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// GPU GEMM:  C[i][jj] = sum_{k<K} A[i][k] * B[jj][k]   (C row-major, ldc)\n// Each output is accumulated by one register chain with k strictly ascending,\n// so the result is bit-identical to a sequential fma loop over k.\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n__global__ void __launch_bounds__(256)\ngemmNTKernel(int M, int N, int K,\n             const double* __restrict__ A, int lda,\n             const double* __restrict__ B, int ldb,\n             double* __restrict__ C, int ldc) {\n    constexpr int TILE = 64;  // output tile edge\n    constexpr int TK = 16;    // k tile\n    __shared__ double As[TK][TILE + 1];\n    __shared__ double Bs[TK][TILE + 1];\n\n    const int tx = threadIdx.x;\n    const int ty = threadIdx.y;\n    const int tid = ty * 16 + tx;\n    const int row0 = blockIdx.y * TILE;\n    const int col0 = blockIdx.x * TILE;\n\n    double acc[4][4];\n#pragma unroll\n    for (int r = 0; r < 4; ++r)\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int c = 0; c < 4; ++c) acc[r][c] = 0.0;\n\n    for (int k0 = 0; k0 < K; k0 += TK) {\n        const int kmax = min(TK, K - k0);\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int t = 0; t < 4; ++t) {\n            const int idx = tid + t * 256;\n            const int r = idx / TK;\n            const int kk = idx % TK;\n            const int gr = row0 + r;\n            const int gc = col0 + r;\n            As[kk][r] = (kk < kmax && gr < M) ? A[static_cast<size_t>(gr) * lda + k0 + kk] : 0.0;\n            Bs[kk][r] = (kk < kmax && gc < N) ? B[static_cast<size_t>(gc) * ldb + k0 + kk] : 0.0;\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n\n        for (int kk = 0; kk < kmax; ++kk) {\n            double a[4], b[4];\n#pragma unroll\n            for (int r = 0; r < 4; ++r) {\n                a[r] = As[kk][ty + 16 * r];\n                b[r] = Bs[kk][tx + 16 * r];\n            }\n#pragma unroll\n            for (int r = 0; r < 4; ++r)\n#pragma unroll\n                for (int c = 0; c < 4; ++c) acc[r][c] = fma(a[r], b[c], acc[r][c]);\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n\n#pragma unroll\n    for (int r = 0; r < 4; ++r) {\n        const int gr = row0 + ty + 16 * r;\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int c = 0; c < 4; ++c) {\n            const int gc = col0 + tx + 16 * c;\n            if (gr < M && gc < N) C[static_cast<size_t>(gr) * ldc + gc] = acc[r][c];\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nvoid gemmNT(int M, int N, int K, const double* A, int lda, const double* B, int ldb,\n            double* C, int ldc) {\n    if (M <= 0 || N <= 0) return;\n    const dim3 block(16, 16);\n    const dim3 grid((N + 63) / 64, (M + 63) / 64);\n    gemmNTKernel<<<grid, block>>>(M, N, K, A, lda, B, ldb, C, ldc);\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Diagonal block of column block [J0, J0+w): finishes L for those columns on the\n// host. Pd holds the partial sums over k < J0 (ld = ldp). Every rank runs this on\n// identical inputs, so all ranks reach the same result (and the same failure).\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\nbool factorDiagonalBlock(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n, const size_t J0,\n                         const size_t w, const double* Pd, const size_t ldp, const bool report) {\n    for (size_t j = 0; j < w; ++j) {\n        const size_t jg = J0 + j;\n        for (size_t i = j; i < w; ++i) {\n            const size_t ig = J0 + i;\n            double sum = Pd[i * ldp + j];\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                sum = std::fma(A[ig * n + J0 + k], A[jg * n + J0 + k], sum);\n            }\n            if (i == j) {\n                const double val = A[jg * n + jg] - sum;\n                if (val <= 0.0) {\n                    // Matrix is not positive definite\n                    if (report) printf(\"Error: Matrix is not positive definite at diagonal element %zu\\n\", jg);\n                    return false;\n                }\n                A[jg * n + jg] = sqrt(val);\n            } else {\n                A[ig * n + jg] = (A[ig * n + jg] - sum) / A[jg * n + jg];\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    return true;\n}\n\n// Blocked left-looking Cholesky. On success the lower triangle of A holds L and the\n// upper triangle is zero. `A` must hold the input matrix on entry (on every rank).\nbool choleskyDecomposition(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n, const Dist& d,\n                           double* dL, double* dP,\n                           std::vector<double>& Pd, std::vector<double>& Pr,\n                           std::vector<double>& pack) {\n    constexpr size_t nb = kPanel;\n\n    for (size_t J0 = 0; J0 < n; J0 += nb) {\n        const size_t J1 = std::min(n, J0 + nb);\n        const size_t w = J1 - J0;\n\n        // Rows below the block split across ranks; the block rows are computed by all.\n        size_t rs = 0, re = 0;\n        partition(J1, n, d.size, d.rank, rs, re);\n        const size_t rc = re - rs;\n\n        // (a) GPU: partial sums over finished columns k < J0, ascending k.\n        gemmNT(static_cast<int>(w), static_cast<int>(w), static_cast<int>(J0),\n               dL + J0 * n, static_cast<int>(n), dL + J0 * n, static_cast<int>(n),\n               dP, static_cast<int>(nb));\n        gemmNT(static_cast<int>(rc), static_cast<int>(w), static_cast<int>(J0),\n               dL + rs * n, static_cast<int>(n), dL + J0 * n, static_cast<int>(n),\n               dP + nb * nb, static_cast<int>(nb));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy2D(Pd.data(), nb * sizeof(double), dP, nb * sizeof(double),\n                                w * sizeof(double), w, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n        if (rc > 0) {\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy2D(Pr.data(), nb * sizeof(double), dP + nb * nb, nb * sizeof(double),\n                                    w * sizeof(double), rc, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n        }\n\n        // (b) Host: finish the diagonal block (identical on every rank).\n        if (!factorDiagonalBlock(A, n, J0, w, Pd.data(), nb, d.rank == 0)) return false;\n\n        // (c) Host (OpenMP): solve for the rows below the block assigned to this rank.\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n        for (size_t t = 0; t < rc; ++t) {\n            const size_t i = rs + t;\n            double* Ai = &A[i * n];\n            for (size_t j = 0; j < w; ++j) {\n                const double* Aj = &A[(J0 + j) * n];\n                double sum = Pr[t * nb + j];\n                for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                    sum = std::fma(Ai[J0 + k], Aj[J0 + k], sum);\n                }\n                Ai[J0 + j] = (Ai[J0 + j] - sum) / Aj[J0 + j];\n            }\n        }\n\n        // (d) MPI: exchange the rows below the block so every rank has the full panel.\n        const size_t rowsBelow = n - J1;\n        if (rowsBelow > 0) {\n            std::vector<int> counts(d.size), displs(d.size);\n            for (int p = 0; p < d.size; ++p) {\n                size_t pb = 0, pe = 0;\n                partition(J1, n, d.size, p, pb, pe);\n                counts[p] = static_cast<int>((pe - pb) * w);\n                displs[p] = static_cast<int>((pb - J1) * w);\n            }\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n            for (size_t t = 0; t < rc; ++t) {\n                for (size_t j = 0; j < w; ++j) {\n                    pack[(rs - J1 + t) * w + j] = A[(rs + t) * n + J0 + j];\n                }\n            }\n            MPI_Allgatherv(MPI_IN_PLACE, 0, MPI_DATATYPE_NULL, pack.data(), counts.data(),\n                           displs.data(), MPI_DOUBLE, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n            for (size_t t = 0; t < rowsBelow; ++t) {\n                for (size_t j = 0; j < w; ++j) {\n                    A[(J1 + t) * n + J0 + j] = pack[t * w + j];\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // (e) Upload the finished block column (rows J0..n) to the GPU for later GEMMs.\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy2D(dL + J0 * n + J0, n * sizeof(double), A.data() + J0 * n + J0,\n                                n * sizeof(double), w * sizeof(double), n - J0,\n                                cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    }\n\n    // Zero out upper triangular part\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = i + 1; j < n; ++j) A[i * n + j] = 0.0;\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\n// Generate a symmetric positive definite matrix (identical values to the sequential\n// generator: B from rand_r, A = B * B^T with a sequential k-sum, plus n on the diagonal).\n// Rows of the lower triangle are split across ranks and exchanged.\nvoid generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n, const Dist& d) {\n    std::vector<double> B(n * n);\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        B[i] = (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 0.5;\n    }\n\n    // Row boundaries balancing the triangular work (row i costs i+1).\n    std::vector<size_t> bnd(d.size + 1);\n    for (int p = 0; p <= d.size; ++p) {\n        bnd[p] = (p == d.size) ? n\n                               : static_cast<size_t>(std::floor(n * std::sqrt(static_cast<double>(p) / d.size)));\n    }\n    const size_t r0 = bnd[d.rank];\n    const size_t r1 = bnd[d.rank + 1];\n\n    std::vector<double> packed(tri(n));\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(dynamic, 4)\n    for (size_t i = r0; i < r1; ++i) {\n        const double* Bi = &B[i * n];\n        double* out = &packed[tri(i)];\n        for (size_t j = 0; j <= i; ++j) {\n            const double* Bj = &B[j * n];\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum = std::fma(Bi[k], Bj[k], sum);\n            }\n            out[j] = sum;\n        }\n        // Add diagonal dominance to ensure positive definiteness\n        out[i] += n;\n    }\n\n    std::vector<int> counts(d.size), displs(d.size);\n    for (int p = 0; p < d.size; ++p) {\n        counts[p] = static_cast<int>(tri(bnd[p + 1]) - tri(bnd[p]));\n        displs[p] = static_cast<int>(tri(bnd[p]));\n    }\n    MPI_Allgatherv(MPI_IN_PLACE, 0, MPI_DATATYPE_NULL, packed.data(), counts.data(), displs.data(),\n                   MPI_DOUBLE, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(dynamic, 16)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j <= i; ++j) A[i * n + j] = packed[tri(i) + j];\n    }\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(dynamic, 16)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = i + 1; j < n; ++j) A[i * n + j] = A[j * n + i];\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateCholesky(const std::vector<double>& L, const std::vector<double>& A_orig, const size_t n) {\n    // Validate by computing L * L^T and comparing with original matrix\n\n    std::vector<double> reconstructed(n * n);\n\n    // Compute L * L^T\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(dynamic, 4)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum += L[i * n + k] * L[j * n + k];\n            }\n            reconstructed[i * n + j] = sum;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Compare with original\n    double maxError = 0.0;\n    double relError = 0.0;\n\n#pragma omp parallel for reduction(max : maxError, relError) schedule(static)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        const double error = fabs(reconstructed[i] - A_orig[i]);\n        maxError = std::max(maxError, error);\n\n        const double rel = error / (fabs(A_orig[i]) + 1e-10);\n        relError = std::max(relError, rel);\n    }\n\n    printf(\"Max absolute error: %.10e\\n\", maxError);\n    printf(\"Max relative error: %.10e\\n\", relError);\n\n    // Check if error is within tolerance\n    if (relError > 1e-6) {\n        printf(\"Validation failed: relative error too large\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Matrix size (default: 512)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint runBenchmark(int argc, char** argv, const Dist& d) {\n    const bool root = (d.rank == 0);\n    size_t n = 512;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            n = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            if (root) printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            if (root) {\n                printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n                printUsage(argv[0]);\n            }\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // The packed lower triangle is exchanged with MPI counts of type int.\n    if (n > 65535) {\n        if (root) printf(\"Matrix size %zu exceeds the supported maximum of 65535\\n\", n);\n        return 1;\n    }\n\n    // Each rank drives one GPU; this benchmark requires CUDA.\n    int numDevices = 0;\n    if (cudaGetDeviceCount(&numDevices) != cudaSuccess || numDevices == 0) {\n        if (root) fprintf(stderr, \"No CUDA devices available; this benchmark requires a GPU\\n\");\n        return 1;\n    }\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaSetDevice(d.localRank % numDevices));\n\n    if (root) {\n        printf(\"Cholesky Decomposition Benchmark\\n\");\n        printf(\"Matrix size: %zu x %zu\\n\", n, n);\n        printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    }\n\n    // Allocate matrix\n    std::vector<double> A(n * n);\n    std::vector<double> A_orig;\n\n    // Generate positive definite matrix\n    if (root) printf(\"Generating positive definite matrix...\\n\");\n    generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(A, n, d);\n\n    if (validate && root) {\n        A_orig = A; // Save original for validation\n    }\n\n    // Workspace (allocated outside the timed region)\n    constexpr size_t nb = kPanel;\n    double* dL = nullptr;\n    double* dP = nullptr;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dL, std::max<size_t>(1, n * n) * sizeof(double)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dP, std::max<size_t>(1, (n + nb) * nb) * sizeof(double)));\n    std::vector<double> Pd(nb * nb), Pr(std::max<size_t>(1, n * nb)), pack(std::max<size_t>(1, n * nb));\n\n    // Perform Cholesky decomposition\n    if (root) printf(\"Computing Cholesky decomposition...\\n\");\n    MPI_Barrier(MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n\n    bool success = choleskyDecomposition(A, n, d, dL, dP, Pd, Pr, pack);\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaDeviceSynchronize());\n\n    MPI_Barrier(MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);\n\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dL));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dP));\n\n    if (!success) {\n        if (root) printf(\"Cholesky decomposition failed\\n\");\n        return 1;\n    }\n\n    if (root) {\n        printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", duration.count());\n\n        // Calculate GFLOPS (approximately n³/3 operations for Cholesky)\n        double ops = (double)n * n * n / 3.0;\n        double gflops = ops / (duration.count() / 1000.0) / 1e9;\n        printf(\"Performance: %.3f GFLOPS\\n\", gflops);\n\n        // Print results for external validation\n        if (printResults) {\n            print_results(A, \"CholeskyL\");\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Validation (root only; the result is identical on every rank)\n    if (validate) {\n        int status = 0;\n        if (root) {\n            printf(\"Validating result...\\n\");\n            const bool valid = validateCholesky(A, A_orig, n);\n            if (valid) {\n                printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n            } else {\n                printf(\"Validation: FAILED\\n\");\n                status = 1;\n            }\n        }\n        return status;\n    }\n\n    return 0;\n}\n\n} // namespace\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    int provided = 0;\n    MPI_Init_thread(&argc, &argv, MPI_THREAD_FUNNELED, &provided);\n\n    Dist d;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &d.rank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &d.size);\n\n    MPI_Comm localComm;\n    MPI_Comm_split_type(MPI_COMM_WORLD, MPI_COMM_TYPE_SHARED, d.rank, MPI_INFO_NULL, &localComm);\n    MPI_Comm_rank(localComm, &d.localRank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(localComm, &d.localSize);\n    MPI_Comm_free(&localComm);\n\n    // Split the node's cores between the ranks sharing it, unless the user set OMP_NUM_THREADS.\n    if (std::getenv(\"OMP_NUM_THREADS\") == nullptr) {\n        long online = sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN);\n        int threads = static_cast<int>(std::max 1L, online / std::max(1, d.localSize)));\n {"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793044518829,"sessionID":"ses_e863e65faffe1w255t7oeq86WJ","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01UCjHTSumbazFjx9LsGYVtU","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r3/cholesky/CMakeLists.txt","content":"cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)\nproject(cholesky_benchmark LANGUAGES CXX CUDA)\n\nset(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)\nset(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)\nset(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD 20)\nset(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)\n\n# Required parallelization stack: MPI (ranks), OpenMP (host threads), CUDA (GPU kernels)\nfind_package(MPI REQUIRED)\nfind_package(OpenMP REQUIRED)\nfind_package(CUDAToolkit REQUIRED)\n\nif(NOT DEFINED CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES)\n    set(CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES native)\nendif()\n\nadd_executable(cholesky cholesky.cpp)\n\n# The source contains CUDA kernels, so it is compiled by the CUDA compiler; the host\n# portions are passed to the host compiler with OpenMP and optimization enabled.\nset_source_files_properties(cholesky.cpp PROPERTIES LANGUAGE CUDA)\nset_target_properties(cholesky PROPERTIES\n    CUDA_ARCHITECTURES \"${CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES}\"\n    LINKER_LANGUAGE CXX)\n\ntarget_compile_options(cholesky PRIVATE\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:-O3>\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:-Xcompiler=-O3>\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:-Xcompiler=-march=native>\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:-Xcompiler=-fopenmp>\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:-Xcompiler=-Wall>\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:-Xcompiler=-Wextra>)\n\ntarget_link_libraries(cholesky PRIVATE\n    MPI::MPI_CXX\n    OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX\n    CUDA::cudart\n    m)\n"},"output":"Wrote file successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"filepath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r3/cholesky/CMakeLists.txt","exists":true,"truncated":false},"title":"home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r3/cholesky/CMakeLists.txt","time":{"start":1793044518787,"end":1793044518797}},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"caller":{"type":"direct"}}},"id":"prt_179c81113001wNC34bWeLoY3pp","sessionID":"ses_e863e65faffe1w255t7oeq86WJ","messageID":"msg_179c80564001dEXWW1GSp5GiKJ"}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793045061242,"sessionID":"ses_e863e65faffe1w255t7oeq86WJ","part":{"id":"prt_179d03273001Wq4gHSdV3xC5eW","messageID":"msg_179d02a95001TgBPRaxTz0iR2u","sessionID":"ses_e863e65faffe1w255t7oeq86WJ","type":"reasoning","text":"Looking at rank 0's timing breakdown, GEMM plus the device-to-host transfer takes about 0.8 seconds on a single GPU, and for two ranks the GEMM work is roughly 0.67s while MPI overhead accounts for 0.2-0.27s including waiting on the other rank's skew. GEMM is clearly the dominant cost, so I'm estimating current throughput at around 225 GFLOPs based on the total FLOP count and single-GPU timing, which suggests room to optimize the kernel.\n\nOddly, each rank's GEMM time barely drops from 0.8s to 0.63-0.67s when splitting across two GPUs, even though each should only handle half the work — I'd expect closer to 0.4s. I'm checking whether this is due to redundant diagonal GEMM computation, low occupancy from small kernels, or synchronization overhead; the ranks are confirmed to use separate GPUs, so I'm digging into grid dimensions, CTA counts versus SM count, and register usage to see if occupancy is limited to just a couple CTAs per SM, with frequent syncthreads calls per k-tile potentially adding overhead.\n\nI'm also weighing shared-memory load efficiency against register blocking strategies, and reasoning that since this GPU runs FP64 at a much reduced rate relative to FP32, the FMA throughput itself is likely the real bottleneck rather than shared memory traffic — meaning the achieved ~40% of peak FP64 throughput is already decent, with limited headroom from further tuning since tensor cores aren't usable here due to the sequential-k dependency. I'm now reconsidering whether the scaling issue instead comes from PCIe transfer overhead or if the redundant diagonal GEMM itself is eating into the expected per-rank speedup.\n\nI estimate the diagonal GEMM's FMA cost is roughly 5% of the full triangular GEMM workload, but suspect its small grid size makes it latency-bound rather than throughput-bound, causing disproportionate wall-clock impact — so I want to directly measure diagonal vs. row GEMM timings separately using cudaEvent instrumentation in a debug build to confirm this hypothesis.\n\n","time":{"start":1793045049971,"end":1793045061135},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

Interestingly, even with np=1 where there's no actual communication, the \"mpi\" section still shows 0.39s, which must just be the pack/unpack loops doing strided host memory copies.\n\nThat seems slow for an 8MB copy per step — probably the real culprit is machine load from 256 OpenMP threads contending with other processes on a heavily loaded box, which inflates all host-parallel sections regardless of my tuning. I could trim work by writing results directly into the pack buffer instead of doing a separate pack loop, then unpacking into A after the allgather since A needs to hold L.\n\nI'm also considering uploading directly from the pack buffer (contiguous rows plus diagonal rows from A) rather than doing a strided cudaMemcpy2D from A, which should be somewhat faster, though the unpack into A would then only be needed at the very end rather than every iteration.\n\nThose savings would only shave off roughly one of three passes. The bigger cost is the MPI section: at np=2 the Allgatherv exchanges around 4MB per step across 64 steps, which should only take about 50ms given both ranks doing symmetric work — but the np=1 timing of 0.39s for pure local pack/unpack seems suspiciously high, suggesting those loops themselves are the real bottleneck.\n\nRunning the numbers, the pack/unpack copies alone total roughly 0.5GB which should take about 0.1s at reasonable memory bandwidth, so the extra time is likely coming from OpenMP barrier overhead under the machine's heavy oversubscription (load of 77 on 256 cores) rather than anything in the algorithm itself — that's noise from other tenants I can't control. Given this, reducing the number of parallel regions and copies seems like the safest improvement, though I should reconsider eliminating the pack/unpack step entirely.\n\nGoing with full host-GPU overlap would be the bigger win but too complex for the remaining budget, so I'll settle for the simpler fix: eliminate one of the three copies by having step (c) write directly into the pack buffer instead of back into A, since unpack will already cover all needed rows.
